brief_item.title: 模拟显示Coding Agent提高任务吞吐但削弱公共知识
brief_item.core_conclusion: 研究用真实GitHub活动初始化1084名开发者，先热身4周，再从同一社区状态分支模拟无Agent和有Agent条件各4周。Agent条件计划任务增加34.0%，完成任务增加39.0%，中位完成时间约从45分钟降至20分钟。
brief_item.mechanism: 模型让开发者代理选择任务和交互，并比较任务路径与公共知识检索。检索基准使用规模匹配的人类语料和Agent语料，衡量知识覆盖、检索步数和成功率。
brief_item.result: 有Agent条件的人际直接交互从32.4%降至11.6%，Agent相关路径升至57.3%。人类语料知识覆盖率为81.1%，Agent语料为22.3%，检索步数从2.63增至8.02。
brief_item.boundary: 这是LLM多Agent仿真，不是线上部署因果证据。采用率、任务和行为依赖提示与模拟设定，未测真实代码正确性、工具延迟或API成本。
brief_item.project_relevance: 任务吞吐提升可能伴随可复用公共上下文变差。基础设施应把决策、测试、理由和仓库摘要保留为结构化产物，并同时测任务时延与成功率，验证这些记录是否改善后续检索的实际效果。

facts.title: From Social Coding to Agentic Coding: Productivity and Relational Reconfiguration in Open-Source Communities
facts.event_hint: arXiv:2608.03585v1 simulates coding-agent adoption in open-source communities and finds a productivity/public-knowledge trade-off
facts.problem: Coding agents may increase individual technical throughput while moving collaboration from visible human-human exchanges into private human-agent loops. It is unclear whether the resulting public records remain useful for later contributors and how adoption gains are distributed across a community.
facts.mechanism: The study builds an LLM-based multi-agent simulation from real GitHub activity and developer-repository relationships. After a historical-commit warm-up, the same community snapshot branches into No-CA and CA conditions for four-week intervention simulations. Developer agents choose tasks and interactions using behavioral profiles, while CA-mediated pathways and a retrieval benchmark compare technical productivity, interaction structure, and the usefulness of public knowledge.

evidence.claim: Introducing coding agents increased planned tasks by 34.0% and completed tasks by 39.0%, while median completion time fell from approximately 45 to 20 minutes versus No-CA.
evidence.condition: Parallel four-week simulation branches from the same warmed-up community state.
evidence.source_locator: PDF pp.1-2, Abstract and simulation results

evidence.claim: Only 26.0% of developers adopted a coding agent by the end of the simulation, and gains concentrated among developers who were already more active and well connected.
evidence.condition: End of four-week CA intervention; adoption is simulated, not observed product telemetry.

evidence.claim: Direct human-human task interaction declined from 32.4% under No-CA to 11.6% under CA; CA-involved modes rose to 57.3%, including 40.3% CA-assisted self-loops.
evidence.condition: Completed-task pathway composition in the parallel simulations.

evidence.claim: On the standardized retrieval benchmark, the real-human corpus achieved 81.1% knowledge coverage versus 22.3% for a size-matched CA corpus; average retrieval steps rose from 2.63 to 8.02 and retrieval success fell from 82.3% to 22.3%.
evidence.condition: Size-matched CA versus real-human public-knowledge corpora on the standardized query benchmark.

evidence.claim: The simulation is initialized with 1,084 continuously active developers and their observed repository relationships, preceded by a four-week warm-up using historical commits.
evidence.condition: LLM-based multi-agent simulation grounded in real GitHub data.

facts.evaluation_context: This is an LLM-based multi-agent simulation, not a controlled field deployment. It uses real GitHub developer/repository data to initialize 1,084 persistent developers, injects historical commits during a four-week warm-up, and branches the same state into No-CA and CA four-week simulations. Retrieval uses a standardized query set over size-matched public-knowledge corpora; the paper also reports pathway composition, adoption, task counts, and completion times.
facts.limitations: Results are model-based simulation outcomes and should not be read as causal evidence from real coding-agent deployments. Developer personas, adoption, task generation, and CA behavior depend on LLM prompts and simulation assumptions; the study does not measure actual repository production, model/API costs, tool-call latency, or code correctness in live communities. The retrieval benchmark captures public-record usefulness under the authors' query/embedding procedure, not all forms of human learning or future-task support. Gains are uneven and short-horizon, with only four-week intervention windows.
facts.project_relevance: The strongest warning for agentic coding infrastructure is that higher task throughput can coexist with worse reusable public context: private CA loops may reduce the durable traces that later agents need for retrieval. This argues for preserving structured decisions, tests, rationale, and repository-level summaries as first-class artifacts while measuring task latency and success; the paper does not provide a concrete indexing or context-compression implementation.
source_notes: Primary arXiv PDF was fetched and the title matches the input metadata exactly.
All quantitative claims are scoped to the LLM simulation, parallel CA/No-CA branches, and the stated retrieval benchmark.
